transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-29 10:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE); Maya Singh (Redwood SE); Luis Ortega (Redwood SRE); Priya Patel (HelioMetrics - Head of ML); Evan Cho (HelioMetrics - Platform Eng); Sophie Lane (HelioMetrics - CTO)

Summary: quick run through of migration strategy, parity checks, and how Redwood Console can orchestrate fallbacks between model variants.

00:00:03 Jordan Park: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and with me Maya our SE and Luis on infra.
00:00:12 Priya Patel: hi thanks, we are excited. we currently run a mix of OpenAI for chat and Together for some fine tuned models and Anthropic for safety checks, it's messy.
00:00:26 Maya Singh: totally, that's what we see a lot. the crosswalk we propose keeps the same calling pattern, we map chat endpoints to Redwood chat API, embeddings to Redwood embeddings, and set up policy routing for safety checks to the Anthropic-equivalent model variant.
00:00:42 Evan Cho: can you clarify policy routing? like if latency spikes can we fall back to cheaper model?
00:00:50 Maya Singh: yeah so typical config is primary model for quality, fallback tier that is slightly quantized or smaller, and region failover. Redwood Console exposes that as route rules you can preview.
00:01:03 Sophie Lane: how much code change? we have about 150 endpoints calling OpenAI-compliant SDK wrappers.
00:01:10 Jordan Park: minimal, we have adapter examples that are drop-in for OpenAI/Anthropic/Together wrapper functions; usually it's env var and a short mapping table. we'll share a repo link after.
00:01:22 Priya Patel: curious on token accounting and cost comparisons, OpenAI charges per token, how do Redwood costs compare?
00:01:31 Maya Singh: depends on hosted vs dedicated. for hosted we show per-token estimates in console; with Dedicated you get predictable throughput and monthly commit. Optimize can suggest batching & cache rules to cut cost 30-60% for chat workloads.
00:01:48 Evan Cho: you mentioned quantization - our main concern is hallucination increasing when we go from fp16 to int8.
00:01:55 Luis Ortega: right we usually test a couple quant profiles and have evaluated quality drop vs token savings; Redwood Optimize suggests recommended quant profile for each model and workload.
00:02:08 Priya Patel: do you support Together's API semantics? they use a different streaming chunk format and function-calling variants...
00:02:17 Maya Singh: streaming shape differences handled by our adapter; function-calling we map via schema translation. sometimes there are edge cases with Together's streaming, we've surfaced those in the parity mapping doc.
00:02:31 Sophie Lane: security --- can we run Redwood Private in our VPC? we need SSO, KMS, and audit logs for compliance.
00:02:40 Jordan Park: yes. Redwood Private supports VPC, customer KMS, and audit log retention; we also have SOC 2 and ISO docs. we'll attach the security packet.
00:02:51 Priya Patel: do you retain input data in hosted mode? we need 30 day retention for debugging but cannot keep customer PII longer than 24 hours.
00:03:00 Maya Singh: hosted has configurable retention; for regulated we recommend Private. for hosted we can configure shorter retention windows per customer.
00:03:10 Evan Cho: on the parity mapping, can you show an example where Together's model that uses dynamic context window maps to Redwood?
00:03:19 Maya Singh: sure, slide 7 in the deck --- we map token limits, chunking, and KV cache expectations. e.g., Together's 32k window maps to Redwood's long-seq profile; we set chunked prefix caching to avoid cache invalidation.
00:03:35 Sophie Lane: what's the downtime or cutover plan? we need a rollback plan if latency or regressions appear.
00:03:43 Luis Ortega: typical approach: start with canary traffic to Redwood Hosted (5-10%), run automated eval prompt set, compare latency and alignment metrics; if pass we increase to dedicated routing and then switch DNS or SDK keys. we keep fallback rules active for 30 days.
00:04:05 Priya Patel: metrics we care about: 99p latency under 1200ms for chat, median cost per turn, and end-to-end safety false positive/negative on our test set.
00:04:17 Maya Singh: we'll include a benchmarking template and the eval harness we used for similar customers.
00:04:25 Evan Cho: about embeddings, we currently use an older OpenAI embedding model. are there differences in vector dim or distance semantics?
00:04:34 Maya Singh: yes dimensions and normalization can differ; Optimize suggests embedding pairing or reindex steps and we have a migration script sample to port vectors or re-embed in a rolling manner.
00:04:50 Priya Patel: can you run a small end-to-end benchmark on Redwood Dedicated? we want throughput numbers with our prompts, 10 tokens per user average.
00:04:59 Jordan Park: yeah we'll spin a dedicated benchmark slot for you; Maya will coordinate dataset and scripts.
00:05:07 Sophie Lane: any gotchas with Together's rate limits? we see bursts.
00:05:12 Maya Singh: Redwood has continuous batching but you can also set burst policies and tokenleak controls; for bursty traffic we recommend dedicated with burst pool.
00:05:25 Evan Cho: competitor question: would switching to Redwood lock us out of some features we use in Anthropic?
00:05:32 Jordan Park: we try to keep parity but sometimes model-specific safety tooling is provider-specific; that's why we propose a hybrid routing step for safety-critical calls until parity is proven.
00:05:45 Priya Patel: ok let's talk specific action items and timeline.
00:05:48 Jordan Park: proposed timeline: week 1 - parity mapping and quick adapter test, week 2 - canary with hosted, week 3 - dedicated perf run, week 4 - rollout.
00:06:00 Maya Singh: I'll send the parity spreadsheet now and we can sync on the prompt set.
00:06:05 Evan Cho: sounds good.
00:06:07 Sophie Lane: thanks all.
00:06:10 Jordan Park: thanks everyone, meeting notes will be in the follow up with links to deck, parity doc, and security packet.

(Transcript continues with Q&A and technical clarifications; some words mis-transcribed, e.g., 'quantize' as 'can ties' at times, 'KV cache' appears as 'K V cache', and occasional speaker labels like Speaker 2 show up in the raw export.)
